title: The Shared Supply Crate
notes: Predict when slice operations share storage and make an independent copy on purpose.
Use an explicit copy when callers should be able to mutate either slice independently.

prompts.title: Listing 4.1 scratchpad
prompts.body: Predict the output. Then change one input and explain the result.
prompts.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	stock := []string{"rope", "torch"}
	front := stock[:1]
	front = append(front, "map")
	fmt.Println(stock) // [rope map]

	owned := make([]string, len(stock))
	copy(owned, stock)
	owned[0] = "ink"
	fmt.Println(stock[0], owned[0]) // rope ink
}
prompts.feedback: Your code draft is saved.

title: The Shared Supply Crate
notes: Answer the checkpoint, then save a code draft for the challenge.

prompts.title: GM checkpoint
prompts.body: What does stock[1] become after appending "map" to stock[:1] in the example?

options.text: The slice index is out of bounds.

prompts.feedback: The shorter slice still has capacity for a second element. append reuses that storage and overwrites the slot stock also sees.
